pages.text: Pipi tapped the sleeping-car window with a beak. "Morning!" Bami pulled the quilt over their head. "A little longer... It's so cozy in here."
Dad peeked in. "You promised to ring the bell before the first toot." "I will... after more sleep..." Bami didn't move and snored again. Only Pipi stamped and chirped outside.
Much later, Bami woke with a start. Sunlight filled the window and the summer sea rushed past. The train was moving already! "My bell? What about my bell?"
Bami went to the cab. "I was supposed to ring it!" Dad smiled. "Pipi called, but you didn't wake, so I did. Getting up isn't hard. Open your eyes and stretch your wings."
Dad stretched up. Bami followed—wings long, legs long! Sleepiness slipped away. "Stretching wakes me right up!" Their eyes grew bright and alert.
Dad whispered, "Then open the window and greet the morning. Stretch before the first toot—that's a conductor's morning." "Like a game!" Bami hopped to the cab window.

Bami pushed it open with their beak. Cool sea air drifted in, and waves greeted them. Pipi landed on the sill. Wings wide, Bami called, "Hello, morning! Stretch before the first toot!" Pipi joined in.
Last, wash your face! Bami dipped into cool washbasin water, rubbed sleep from their eyes, and cleaned their face feathers. "I started my morning myself!" They shook off the drops.

Now Bami knew the steps. "One, wake to Pipi and stretch! Two, open the window and greet morning! Three, wash in cool water!" Next day, before Pipi called, Bami hopped up and pulled the bell rope with a foot. Ding!
Toot! The train started. Holding the big handle with a foot, Dad cuddled Bami with one wing. "Right on time! Up bright as the morning sun!" Stretch before the first toot!
